cases.what_created: Edison's Pearl Street Station in New York began supplying electricity to customers.
cases.source: Hughes, T. P., Networks of Power: Electrification in Western Society, 1880-1930 (Johns Hopkins, 1983).

cases.what_created: New York and Wisconsin set up state commissions to regulate utility rates and service.
cases.source: Hughes, T. P., Networks of Power (Johns Hopkins, 1983).

cases.what_created: Insull utility holding-company empire collapsed, wiping out many small investors.
cases.source: McDonald, F., Insull (University of Chicago Press, 1962).

cases.what_created: Public Utility Holding Company Act and Federal Power Act brought holding companies and interstate power under federal oversight.
cases.source: Public Utility Holding Company Act of 1935; Federal Power Act of 1935 (49 Stat. 803, 838).

cases.what_created: Rural Electrification Administration financed power lines to farms that private utilities had skipped.
cases.source: Executive Order 7037 (1935); Rural Electrification Act of 1936.

cases.what_created: Northeast blackout left about 30 million people without power.
cases.source: Federal Power Commission, Prevention of Power Failures (1967).

cases.what_created: Utilities formed the voluntary National Electric Reliability Council (now NERC).
Northeast blackout affected about 50 million people in the US and Canada.
cases.source: US-Canada Power System Outage Task Force, Final Report on the August 14, 2003 Blackout (2004).

cases.what_created: Energy Policy Act of 2005 made reliability standards mandatory and enforceable.
cases.source: Energy Policy Act of 2005, Public Law 109-58, section 1211.
